1: [Yasna 29:1-2 — The cry of the soul of the cow]

The soul of the cow cried out: For whom did you create me, and for what purpose? Fury and violence, rapine and insolence weigh me down. Give me a herdsman who is a prayerful man. And the Maker of the cow answered: There is no herdsman who is without malice.

Then the Holy Spirit and the Archangels and the angel of the cow consulted together, and they chose Zarathustra, the son of Spitama, as the one who shall give voice to the praises of the Wise Lord. And he wept at the weight of it, and the Lord said: Go, for I have made you able.

Hear with your ears the best things; look upon them with clear-seeing thought, for decision between the two faiths, each man for himself. Know that the two spirits in the beginning of the world are twins, and they are Good and Evil in thought, in word, and in deed. Choose the good between them, and the choosing is yours alone.

When the retribution comes for the deeds of the wicked, then, O Wise Lord, at Thy command shall the good ruler establish his kingdom with the power of the molten metal, to give the final decision among the living.
2: Through the tongue speak the words of good and ill, and through the hands act — for the tongue and the hand are the two messengers of the mind. And the wise man uses both for righteousness, and the wicked for the lie.
[Yasna 34:2 — The reward of the good mind]

I ask Thee for the best of rewards, O Wise Lord, through the good mind: the reward which is the longing of the soul. Teach me, Lord, the paths of righteousness, that I may speak as one who has seen, and act as one who has understood.

As the very first of all was the vision, so was the word: I saw Thee, O Wise Lord, as the first of all things, the father of the good mind, the true fashioner of righteousness, who founded all things at the beginning.
3: Now shall I speak of the greatest of all teachings, which the Wise Lord taught me: the truth is the word of the good mind. Whoever gives ear to the teachings of righteousness shall come to long ages of joy and peace.

I know the words of the prayer, O Wise Lord, but my house is empty of cattle and empty of men. My foes press upon me. Bring me, therefore, the wealth of the good mind, and the feast of righteousness, and let Thy kingdom come with power.

In the last days the mountains shall give way and the valleys be exalted; the dead shall rise, and the world shall be made new. Evil shall be burned out like stubble, and the light shall have no shadow, and the earth shall be the earth as the Maker intended it — and that day is not far, for the seed of it is sown in every act of truth.
